title: Dashboard UX and micro-SLI design notes for inference
content:
Purpose:
This note captures pragmatic guidance for designing dashboards and micro-SLIs for Redwood inference services. Focus is on making dashboards that are readable at-a-glance, actionable for oncall, and structured so that product engineers can quickly map a symptom -> hypothesis -> remediation.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to hosted API / dedicated / private inference endpoints (same UX principles, but different data availability).
- Goal is low-noise, high-signal dashboards for day-to-day ops and incident response. Not an exhaustive metrics catalog.
- Assumes metric ingestion with tags: request_id, customer_id (hashed), model_family, model_version, deployment_zone, routing_policy, batch_size, has_kv_cache, response_tokens.

Design principles (high level):
1) Surface the user-visible experience first: P95/P99 tail latency for end-to-end request (client-obs) + errors + success rate.
2) Decompose into independent micro-SLIs that map to probable root causes (runtime, routing, infra, model).
3) Keep the top panel small: 4–6 widgets with clear thresholds; everything else is drilldown.
4) Avoid alert fatigue: prefer compound conditions (e.g., sustained increase in end-to-end latency AND increased model compute latency).
5) Use consistent color/lexicon across dashboards (green/yellow/red bands, "degraded" vs "failed").
6) Include cost signals in drilldown so engineers can trade latency vs cost during triage.

Micro-SLI recommendations (names are intentionally concrete):
- consumer_e2e_latency_ms_p95: end-to-end latency as observed by API front door, p95 over 1m/5m windows.
- compute_step_latency_ms_p95: time spent in the serving runtime (kernel + decode) p95.
- kv_cache_hit_rate_1m: fraction of requests served with a valid KV/prefix cache hit.
- batch_formation_delay_ms_p95: time waiting for batch assembly before the first token is produced.
- request_queue_depth: current queued requests per worker shard.
- stubbed_fallback_rate: fraction of requests that fell back to cheaper model variant due to routing policy.
- token_generation_rps: tokens produced per second per model_family (useful for cost curves).
- successful_responses_ratio: 2xx/total requests, broken down by model_version.
- grpc_stream_resets_rate: number of stream resets or client disconnects per 1k requests.

Alerting guidance (rules and thresholds):
- Incident-level alert (P0): consumer_e2e_latency_ms_p99 > 3x baseline sustained for 3 minutes OR successful_responses_ratio < 95% for 2 minutes.
- P1 (investigate): compute_step_latency_ms_p95 increased >50% relative to rolling 7d baseline AND batch_formation_delay_ms_p95 < baseline (indicates compute hot-spot).
- P2 (inform): kv_cache_hit_rate_1m drops >20% absolute and sustained for 10 minutes.
- Avoid single-metric noisy alerts: require at least one corroborating signal (error spikes, queue depth, resource saturation).
- Create customer-impacted alert variants (annotate with customer_id top-n) for billing-sensitive customers.

Dashboard layout suggestions (top-down):
1) Top row: single-line summary widgets (heat map for latency by region/model_family, SLI sparklines for the past 1h) + traffic/cost overview.
2) Second row: consumer experience panel (e2e latency p50/p95/p99, success ratio, errors with HLL counts of customer_id).
3) Third row: serving runtime panel (compute_step_latency p50/p95, GPU utilization percentiles, batch size distribution, kv cache hit rate).
4) Fourth row: routing & fallback (routing decisions by policy, fallback rate, capacity-bumps/bursts).
5) Bottom row: supporting panels (trace waterfall sample, recent heavy traces list, token cost histogram).

Widget examples & queries (pseudo):
- E2E latency P95 by model: timeseries: redwood.requests.latency.p95_ms{env:prod} by model_family
- Compute vs wait split: stacked area: redwood.requests.stage_latency_ms{stage:compute} and {stage:queue} stacked to show proportion.
- Cache hit rate: ratio(redwood.kv.cache.hits, redwood.kv.cache.requests) rolling 1m.
- Heavy traces table: top-20 traces by compute_step_latency with columns [trace_id, model_version, batch_size, response_tokens, sample_link].

Tracing and explorer ergonomics:
- Sampling: preserve 100% traces for high-severity errors; for normal ops ~1% uniform sampling + targeted 100% for requests above p99 latency or above tokens threshold.
- Span design: keep spans coarse-grained and stable: front_door -> router -> batcher -> runtime_kernel -> decode. Each span should include tags: model_family, model_version, routing_policy, batch_size, kv_cache_hit (bool), customer_id_hash.
- Link traces to dashboard: heavy traces widget should include a direct link to the trace viewer with filter pre-applied.
- Session view for multi-step interactions: aggregate traces by conversation_id to see time spent per turn (useful for chat flows).

Instrumentation checklist (to implement before dashboard rollout):
- Ensure all requests emit request_id and trace_id and both are carried in logs, metrics, traces.
- Add model_version and routing_policy tags to request-level metrics.
- Emit latency broken down by logical stage with consistent units (ms).
- Emit batch_size and response_token_count as histograms (use exemplar linking to traces for heavy buckets).
- Emit a short-lived counter for "fallback_reason" counts (labelled by reason).

UX considerations for oncall vs product:
- Oncall dashboard should default to last 15m window; product/analytics default to 24h.
- Provide one-click filters to limit to a customer_id (hashed) for escalations.
- Use a single canonical dashboard per service; create minimal per-model variant views for experiments only.

Rollout checklist / quick win changes (next 3 sprints):
- Sprint 1: implement micro-SLI metrics + p95/p99 aggregation, create top-row summary widgets.
- Sprint 2: add heavy traces widget and exemplar linking from histogram buckets.
- Sprint 3: implement alert rules with compound conditions and test in staging.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Sampling cost vs visibility: how many p99 traces do we store centrally? Can we offload detailed trace storage to S3 for ad-hoc retrieval?
- Customer privacy: hashed customer ids are OK, but what about traces that contain PII in prompts? Need automatic redaction before indexing.
- Micro-SLI proliferation: How many micro-SLIs do we allow before the top-level becomes noisy? Proposal: cap primary SLI panel to 6 signals.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Put together a brief demo video showing triage flow from e2e alert -> drilldown -> trace. @Arjun to own demo recording.
- Lina: sketch final dashboard wireframe (Figma) with annotated drilldown paths.
- Ethan: spike on exemplar linking from histogram buckets to traces.

References and inspiration:
- internal: CONFLUENCE-OBS-UX-142 (dashboard style guide)
- external: "Practical Monitoring" book notes for SLI decomposition (informal)

End.
